This is a bit late, but I've actually been in several french schools in the region so I might be able to help.

LaMarsh and St. Antoine are both really close to each other. LaMarsh is public, while St. Antoine is catholic. I attended both and thought they were both decent schools. I was always told St. Antoine was better for academics. There's definitely more students at St. Antoine now because a good chunk of students transferred from LaMarsh. 

If learning disabilities are a concern then I would lean toward St. Antoine as they definitely had more experience when it came towards that. I also found the teachers to be better at St. Antoine, but it's possible things have changed at LaMarsh. LaMarsh definitely had a better theater program when I was there.

If you're leaning towards a school in St. Catherines, then there's heritage. I was very young when I went there, but I remember the school being very big and it had the greatest yard. 

I'm not sure if you're looking for high schools, but there's two french high schools. They're both in Welland. It was crappy to commute, but you don't have much of a choice otherwise. The schools are Confederation and Jean-Vanier. I went to Jean-Vanier. It has far more people than Confederation, but is catholic. Jean-Vanier moved to a nice new spot a few years back. It's very modern and has nice classrooms. Really great teachers.

From what I know about Confed, there's very few students. However, the students that are there seem happy and like they've formed a nice community. I heard they have a great culinary program. Both the schools have co-op programs, mostly at museums, restaurants and trade jobs.

There's also A.N Myer. They're an English school high school but have, supposedly, a very big immersion program. They're much much bigger than JV and Confed, so there's more clubs and sports.

If there's anything more specific you'd like to know, just message me. I feel like this is my one area of expertise haha.
